subject: Residency carveouts for EU customers — Privatelink pathing & evidence request
messages:
From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@medsyshealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eugene Park <e.park@consult-audit.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data residency clarifications + privatelink evidence needed

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. As we prep the submission to our internal compliance committee, they have two narrowly scoped asks so we can sign off on hosting in the EU: 

1) A clear statement of any carveouts (if any) where traffic or logs may traverse or be processed outside the EU and why — we need the technical justification and mitigation controls.
2) A diagram and short runbook for the privatelink/Private VPC path that proves no egress crosses non-EU public networks (we're specifically trying to avoid multi-hop public egress during inference).

Could you provide an evidence packet (diagram + one-page runbook + SOC2 snapshot) by EOD Thursday (June 3)? If you have a template or a short checklist we can include in our change request, that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — this is the last gating item for our Prod pilot.

Best,
Sofia
Legal Ops — MedSys Health

[attachment: compliance-ask_MSH.pdf]
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@medsyshealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency clarifications + privatelink evidence needed

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear asks. We can deliver the packet you described. Summary of what we'll provide: 

- Residencies and carveouts: a concise statement that our EU-hosted Private deployment keeps inference compute and KV caches within EU regions; the only cross-border exceptions are asynchronous metrics ingestion to our central analytics (optional) and limited S3-based archive exports initiated by customer ops when requested. Both have encryption/controls and can be disabled.
- Privatelink pathing: a peering diagram showing customer VPC -> privatelink + dedicated peering -> EU-only egress nodes, and a one-page runbook describing connection verification and fallback (canary routing to dedicated EU pool).
- SOC 2 snapshot: redacted pages covering boundary and access control (we'll include the April 2026 snapshot).

We'll attach the diagram and runbook as separate artifacts. Proposed delivery: initial packet tomorrow EOD (May 30) for your review, final by June 2. If June 3 is a hard deadline we can prioritize.

Looping in Irene to confirm the SOC2 export and Marcus for the peering diagram.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-05-30T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency clarifications + privatelink evidence needed

Sofia / Aditya —

I've pulled the SOC 2 snapshot (redacted) and added a short cover note that highlights the control sections most relevant to residency and privatelink: boundary scoping, network segregation, and key management. See attached: "soc2-snapshot-2026-04.pdf".

On the carveouts: to be explicit for the committee, the potential non-EU flows are:
- Optional telemetry export to central analytics (can be disabled per-customer via account config).
- Outbound archive exports when customer explicitly requests exports to a non-EU storage target (documented, audited).

Mitigations included: per-tenant flag to disable telemetry, enforced EU-only egress policy on the EU dedicated pool, and HSM-backed key access control.

I'll also attach a short attestation paragraph you can include in your packet.

Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

[attachment: soc2-snapshot-2026-04.pdf]
From: marcus_lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia.alvarez@medsyshealth.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, irene_choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency clarifications + privatelink evidence needed

Sofia —

Attached are two artifacts: 1) redwood-privatelink-path-diagram.pdf, and 2) privatelink-connection-runbook-v1.md (one-page). Key notes: 

- The peering path is customer VPC -> AWS Privatelink endpoint (EU region) -> dedicated Redwood peering fabric -> EU-only serving pool (pinned to eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 depending on customer selection). No public internet hops in normal flow.
- Fallback behavior: if EU pool capacity is constrained, automated routing will fallback to a compatible EU-based quantized model in the standby EU pool; we do not fallback to non-EU pools unless the customer explicitly enables cross-region fallback.
- Verification steps: traceroute on the privatelink endpoint, checking our peering BGP session state, and validating the TTL/hops; included in runbook.

Next actions: please confirm whether you want the runbook expanded into an operational playbook (30–45 minute task) or leave as-is for the compliance packet.

Marcus Lin
Network Architecture — Redwood Inference

[attachment: redwood-privatelink-path-diagram.pdf]

Aditya / team —

Thank you, this is exactly what we needed. Eugene (our external auditor) confirms the artifacts look sane; he will run the peering diagram through a quick check tomorrow.

Two small follow-ups: 
- Can you add a single-line statement confirming that the KV cache used during inference is not replicated outside the EU for this deployment?
- Please provide the short attestation paragraph Irene mentioned as a plain text snippet we can paste into our internal change request.

If you can send those two items by EOD Monday (June 7) we'll be able to close the committee review and move to pilot.

Best,
Sofia
